translations.literal: Commandant the clansman Jiuzhu, deputy commandant Wang Jian, and overall leader Wang Fuyin with three thousand five hundred Divine Arm troops; left-wing marshal the clansman Xiaoloushi with one thousand Personal Guard troops; right-wing marshal Wanyan Anchuhu with one thousand Personal Guard troops; overall leader Wanyan Changle and deputy commander Wenden Changsun with three hundred horse; Prince of Jun Wang Yishen with one hundred fifty horse; Prince of Jun Fanchengjin and overall leader Su Yuansungui with three thousand troops—all subordinate to overall commander Baijia.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant the clansman Jiuzhu, Deputy Commandant Wang Jian, and Overall Leader Wang Fuyin with 3,500 Divine Arm troops; Left-wing Marshal Xiaoloushi with 1,000 guards; Right-wing Marshal Anchuhu with 1,000 guards; Overall Leader Wanyan Changle and Deputy Commander Wenden Changsun with 300 horse; Prince Wang Yishen with 150 horse; Prince Fanchengjin and Overall Leader Su Yuansungui with 3,000 men—all under Overall Commander Baijia.

sentences.zh: 飛騎都尉兼合里合總領術虎只魯歡、總領夾谷得伯、颭軍田衆家奴等百人及諸臣下，發京師。

translations.literal: Flying-cavalry commandant and concurrently Helihe overall leader Shuhu Zhiluhuan, overall leader Jiagu Debo, standard-bearer Tian Zhongjianu, and a hundred others together with the various ministers below set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Flying-cavalry Commandant and Helihe Overall Leader Shuhu Zhiluhuan, Overall Leader Jiagu Debo, standard-bearer Tian Zhongjianu, a hundred others, and the court set out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲辰，車駕至黃陵岡，白撒先降大兵兩寨，得河朔降將，上赦之，授以印及金虎符。

translations.literal: On jiachen of the twelfth month the imperial carriage reached Huangling Mound. Baisa had first surrendered two camps of the great army and obtained surrendered generals from north of the river; the emperor pardoned them and gave them seals and golden tiger tallies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day of the twelfth month the court reached Huangling Mound. Baisa had first accepted the surrender of two enemy camps and gained Hebei defectors; the emperor pardoned them and gave seals and golden tiger tallies.

sentences.zh: 群臣議以河朔諸將前導，鼓行入開州，取大名、東平，豪傑當有回應者，破竹之勢成矣。

translations.literal: The ministers debated having the Hebei generals lead the way, marching with drums into Kaizhou, taking Daming and Dongping; local heroes would surely respond, and a bamboo-splitting momentum would be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued that Hebei generals should lead the march with drums into Kaizhou, take Daming and Dongping, and rouse local heroes in an irresistible advance.

sentences.zh: 溫敦昌孫曰：「太后、中宮皆在南京，北行萬一不如意，聖主孤身欲何所爲？

translations.literal: Wenden Changsun said: "The empress dowager and the central palace are both at Nanjing. If the northern march should by chance go wrong, what could the sacred sovereign do alone?
translations.idiomatic: Wenden Changsun said: "The empress dowager and consort are both at Nanjing. If the northern march goes wrong, what can the emperor do alone?

sentences.zh: 若往歸德，更五六月不能還京。

translations.literal: If we go to Guide, five or six more months will pass without returning to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: If we go to Guide, five or six more months will pass without returning to the capital.

sentences.zh: 不如先取衛州，還京爲便。」

translations.literal: It would be better first to take Weizhou and then return to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better first to take Weizhou and then return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 白撒奏曰：「聖體不便鞍馬，且不可令大兵知上所在，今可駐歸德。

translations.literal: Baisa memorialized: "The sacred person is not suited to horseback, and the great army must not be allowed to know where Your Majesty is; for now we can halt at Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa memorialized: "Your Majesty is not fit for the saddle, and the enemy must not learn where you are; halt at Guide for now.

sentences.zh: 臣等率降將往東平，俟諸軍至，可一鼓而下，因而經略河朔，且空河南之軍。」

translations.literal: We will lead the surrendered generals to Dongping. When the armies arrive, it can be taken with one drumbeat; then we can manage Heshuo and also empty Henan of enemy troops."
translations.idiomatic: We will lead the surrendered generals to Dongping. When the armies arrive, it can be taken with one drumbeat; then we can manage Heshuo and also empty Henan of enemy troops."

sentences.zh: 上以爲然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時上已遣官奴將三百騎探漚麻岡未還，上將御船，賜白撒劍，得便宜從事，決東平之策。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had already sent Guan Nu with three hundred horsemen to reconnoiter Oumagang and they had not returned. The emperor was about to board ship, bestowed a sword on Baisa with discretionary authority, and settled on the Dongping plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent Guan Nu with three hundred horse to scout Oumagang and awaited his return. About to board ship, he gave Baisa a sword with discretionary authority and committed to the Dongping plan.

sentences.zh: 官奴還奏衛州，有糧可取？

translations.literal: Guan Nu returned and reported: "At Weizhou, is there grain that can be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Nu returned and reported: "Is there grain to be had at Weizhou?"

sentences.zh: 上召白撒問之，白撒曰：「京師且不能守，就得衛州，欲何爲耶？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Baisa to ask him. Baisa said: "The capital cannot even be held—even if we got Weizhou, what would we do?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Baisa, who said: "We cannot even hold the capital—what good is Weizhou?

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，東平之策爲便。」

translations.literal: As I see it, the Dongping plan is more convenient."
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, the Dongping plan is more convenient."

sentences.zh: 上主官奴之議。

translations.literal: The emperor upheld Guan Nu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Guan Nu.

sentences.zh: 明年正月朔，次黃陵岡。

translations.literal: On the new moon of the first month of the following year they halted at Huangling Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On the new year's day of the following year they halted at Huangling Mound.

sentences.zh: 是日，歸德守臣以糧糗三百餘船來餉，遂就其舟以濟南岸，未濟者萬人，大元將回古乃率四千騎追擊之，賀都喜揮一黃旗督戰，身中十六七箭，軍殊死鬥，得卒十餘人，大兵少卻。

translations.literal: That day the Guide defending officials brought more than three hundred grain boats as provisions; they then used those boats to cross to the south bank. Ten thousand had not yet crossed when the Great Yuan general Huigu Nai led four thousand horsemen in pursuit. Heduxi waved a yellow flag to direct the battle, was struck by sixteen or seventeen arrows, and the army fought to the death, bringing off a little more than ten soldiers before the great army drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: That day Guide officials brought more than three hundred grain boats; the court used them to cross the south bank. Ten thousand men were still on the north bank when Great Yuan general Huigu Nai pursued with four thousand horse. Heduxi waved a yellow flag to command the fight, took sixteen or seventeen arrows, and his men fought to the death, saving a dozen soldiers before the enemy drew back slightly.

sentences.zh: 上遣送酒百壺勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a hundred jars of wine to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a hundred jars of wine to reward them.

sentences.zh: 須臾，北風大作，舟皆吹著南岸，諸兵復擊之，溺死者近千人，元帥豬兒、都尉紇石烈訛論等死之。

translations.literal: In a moment a north wind rose fiercely; the boats were all blown back to the south bank, and the troops struck them again; nearly a thousand drowned. Marshal Zhuer, commandant Heshenlie Elun, and others died.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a fierce north wind blew the boats back to the south bank; the enemy struck again, and nearly a thousand drowned. Marshal Zhuer, Commandant Heshenlie Elun, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 建威都尉完顏訛論出降於大元。

translations.literal: Jianwei commandant Wanyan Elun came out and surrendered to Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwei Commandant Wanyan Elun surrendered to the Great Yuan.

sentences.zh: 上於北岸望之震懼，率從官爲豬兒等設祭，哭之，皆贈官，錄用其子侄，斬訛論出二弟以徇。

translations.literal: On the north bank the emperor watched, shaken with fear; he led his attendants to set out offerings for Zhuer and the others, wept for them, posthumously enfeoffed them all, enrolled their sons and nephews in office, and beheaded Elunchu's two younger brothers as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from the north bank, the emperor was shaken with fear; he led attendants in mourning rites for Zhuer and the others, posthumously enfeoffed them, enrolled their sons and nephews, and executed Elunchu's two younger brothers as a warning.

sentences.zh: 遂命白撒攻衛州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Baisa to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Wanyan Baisa to attack Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 上駐兵河上，留親衛軍三千護從，都尉高顯步軍一萬，元帥官奴忠孝軍一千，郡王范成進、王義深、上党公張開、元帥劉益等軍總帥百家總之，各齎十日糧，聽承裔節制。

translations.literal: The emperor encamped his troops on the river; he left three thousand Personal Guards to escort him, Commandant Gao Xian's ten thousand foot soldiers, Marshal Guan Nu's thousand Zhongxiao troops, and the armies of Princes Fan Chengjin and Wang Yishen, Shangdang Duke Zhang Kai, Marshal Liu Yi, and others—overall commander Bai Jia commanded them all; each carried ten days' rations and was placed under Chengyi's control.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted on the riverbank, leaving three thousand Personal Guards as escort, ten thousand foot under Commandant Gao Xian, a thousand Zhongxiao troops under Marshal Guan Nu, and the forces of Princes Fan Chengjin and Wang Yishen, Shangdang Duke Zhang Kai, Marshal Liu Yi, and others—all under overall commander Bai Jia, each man carrying ten days' grain and subject to Chengyi's orders.

sentences.zh: 發自蒲城，上時已遣賽不將馬軍北向矣，白撒以三十騎追及，謂賽不曰：「有旨，命我將馬軍。」

translations.literal: Setting out from Pucheng, the emperor had already sent Saibu north at the head of the cavalry; Baisa with thirty horsemen overtook him and said to Saibu: "There is an edict appointing me to command the cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: They marched out from Pucheng. The emperor had already sent Wanyan Saibu north with the horse; Baisa overtook him with thirty riders and said, "I have orders to take command of the cavalry."

sentences.zh: 賽不謂上曰：「北行議已決，不可中變。」

translations.literal: Saibu said to the emperor: "The decision to march north has been settled; it cannot be changed midway."
translations.idiomatic: Saibu told the emperor, "The northern march is already decided—it cannot be reversed midway."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「丞相當與平章和同。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The chief minister and the participation councillor should act in harmony."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The chief minister and the participation councillor must agree."

sentences.zh: 完顏仲德持御馬銜苦諫曰：「存亡在此一舉，衛州決不可攻。」

translations.literal: Wanyan Zhongde, gripping the imperial horse's bridle, remonstrated bitterly: "Survival or ruin hangs on this one move—Weizhou must on no account be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zhongde seized the bridle of the imperial horse and pleaded urgently: "The fate of the dynasty rests on this decision—Weizhou must not be attacked."

sentences.zh: 上麾之曰：「參政不知。」

translations.literal: The emperor waved him off and said: "The participation councillor does not understand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waved him away. "The participation councillor does not understand."

sentences.zh: 白撒遂攻衛州，兵至城下，御旗黃傘招之不下。

translations.literal: Baisa then attacked Weizhou; when the troops reached the foot of the walls, the imperial banner and yellow parasol summoned surrender, but the city would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa attacked Weizhou anyway. When his men reached the walls, the imperial banner and yellow parasol called for surrender, but the city would not yield.

sentences.zh: 其夜，北騎三千奄至，官奴、和速嘉兀地不、按出虎與之戰，北兵卻六十里。

translations.literal: That night three thousand northern horsemen arrived suddenly; Guan Nu, Hesujia Wudibu, and Anchuhu fought them, and the northern army fell back sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: That night three thousand northern riders appeared without warning. Guan Nu, Hesujia Wudibu, and Anchuhu met them in battle and drove the northerners back sixty li.

sentences.zh: 然自發蒲城，遷延八日始至衛，而猝無攻具，縛槍爲雲梯。

translations.literal: Yet from the departure at Pucheng they had delayed eight days before reaching Wei, and suddenly had no siege equipment; they bound spears to make scaling ladders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Pucheng they had dawdled eight days before reaching Wei, and arrived with no siege gear—spears were lashed together for scaling ladders.

sentences.zh: 州人知不能攻，守益嚴。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture knew they could not be taken and defended all the more strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the assault could not succeed, the defenders tightened their guard.

sentences.zh: 凡攻三日不克。

translations.literal: In all they attacked three days without success.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted the city three days without success.

sentences.zh: 及聞河南大兵濟自張家渡，至衛西南，遂班師。

translations.literal: When they heard that the great army of Henan had crossed from Zhangjia Ford and reached the southwest of Wei, they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that the main northern force had crossed at Zhangjia Ford and was southwest of Wei; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大兵踵其後，戰于白公廟，敗績，白撒等棄軍遁，劉益、張開皆爲民家所殺。

translations.literal: The great army followed on their heels; they fought at Baigong Temple and were utterly defeated; Baisa and the others abandoned the army and fled; Liu Yi and Zhang Kai were both killed by local households.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy followed close behind. At Baigong Temple they were routed; Baisa and others abandoned the army and fled. Liu Yi and Zhang Kai were killed by civilians along the way.

sentences.zh: 車駕還次蒲城東三十里，白撒使人密奏劉益一軍叛去。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted thirty li east of Pucheng on the return; Baisa sent someone to report secretly that Liu Yi's army had mutinied and gone off.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train halted thirty li east of Pucheng on the return march. Baisa secretly reported that Liu Yi's command had deserted.

sentences.zh: 點檢抹撚兀典、總領溫敦昌孫時侍行帳中，請上登舟，上曰：「正當決戰，何遽退乎？」

translations.literal: Inspector Mozhen Wudian and Chief Steward Wudun Changsun were then attending in the traveling tent and asked the emperor to board ship; the emperor said: "This is precisely the moment for a decisive battle—why withdraw in haste?"
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Mozhen Wudian and Chief Steward Wudun Changsun, attending in the traveling tent, urged the emperor aboard ship. He said, "This is the moment to fight—why retreat so soon?"

sentences.zh: 少頃，白撒至，倉皇言於上曰：「今軍已潰，大兵近在堤外，請聖主幸歸德。」

translations.literal: In a little while Baisa arrived and, in panic, said to the emperor: "The army has now collapsed; the great army is close outside the dike—may Your Majesty proceed to Guide."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Baisa arrived in disarray and told the emperor, "The army is broken; the enemy is at the dike—Your Majesty must go to Guide."

sentences.zh: 上遂登舟，侍衛皆不知，巡警如故。

translations.literal: The emperor then boarded ship; the guards all knew nothing of it, and patrols continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor boarded at once. His guards knew nothing; patrols continued as usual.

sentences.zh: 時夜已四更矣，遂狼狽入歸德。

translations.literal: The night had already reached the fourth watch; thus in disarray they entered Guide.
translations.idiomatic: It was already the fourth watch. They reached Guide in disorder.

sentences.zh: 白撒收潰兵大橋，得二萬餘人，懼不敢入。

translations.literal: Baisa gathered the routed troops at Daqiao and got a little more than twenty thousand men, but in fear he dared not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa rallied the fugitives at Daqiao—more than twenty thousand men—but dared not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣近侍局提點移剌粘古、紇石烈阿里合、護衛二人以舟往迎之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sent Palace Attendants Bureau Commissioner Yila Niangu, Heshenlie Alihe, and two guards by boat to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the emperor sent Palace Attendants Commissioner Yila Niangu, Heshenlie Alihe, and two guards by boat to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 既至，不聽入見，並其子下獄。

translations.literal: When they arrived he would not grant an audience and put him in prison together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived he refused to see Baisa and imprisoned him together with his son.

sentences.zh: 諸都尉司軍以白撒不戰而退，發憤出怨言。

translations.literal: The troops of the various commandant offices, because Baisa had retreated without fighting, vented their anger in complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of the commandant offices, furious that Baisa had fled without fighting, broke into open complaint.

sentences.zh: 上乃暴其罪曰：「惟汝將士，明聽朕言：我初提大軍次黃陵岡得捷，白撒即奏宜渡河取衛州，可得糧十萬石，乘勝恢復河北。

translations.literal: The emperor then exposed his crimes, saying, "You officers and soldiers, clearly hear my words: When I first led the great army to Huangling Mound and won victory, Baisa immediately memorialized that we should cross the river and take Weizhou, where we could obtain one hundred thousand shi of grain and use the victory to recover Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then exposed his crimes, saying, "You officers and soldiers, clearly hear my words: When I first led the great army to Huangling Mound and won victory, Baisa immediately memorialized that we should cross the river and take Weizhou, where we could obtain one hundred thousand shi of grain and use the victory to recover Hebei.

sentences.zh: 我從其計，令率諸軍攻衛。

translations.literal: I followed his plan and ordered him to lead the armies in attacking Wei.
translations.idiomatic: I followed his advice and ordered him to lead the attack on Wei.

sentences.zh: 去蒲城二百余里，白撒遷延八日方至，又不預備攻具，以致敗衄。

translations.literal: Though only a little more than two hundred li from Pucheng, Baisa delayed eight days before arriving, and again failed to prepare siege equipment, so that defeat followed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Weizhou lay only two hundred-odd li from Pucheng, Baisa took eight days to reach it and brought no siege equipment—hence our defeat.

sentences.zh: 白撒棄軍竄還蒲城，便言諸軍已潰，北兵勢大不可當，信從登舟，幾死于水。

translations.literal: Baisa abandoned the army and fled back to Pucheng, then at once said the armies had collapsed and the northern troops' momentum was too great to withstand; believing him, I boarded ship and nearly perished in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa abandoned the army and fled to Pucheng, then claimed our forces had collapsed and the northerners were unstoppable. I believed him, boarded ship, and nearly drowned.

sentences.zh: 若當時知諸軍未嘗潰，只河北戰死，亦可垂名於後。

translations.literal: Had I then known the armies had never collapsed and had only died fighting in Hebei, our names could still have been handed down to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Had I known the army was not broken and had only died fighting for Hebei, our names might still stand in history.

sentences.zh: 今白撒已下獄，不復錄用，籍其家產以賜汝衆，其盡力國家，無效此人。」

translations.literal: Now Baisa has been imprisoned, will never again be employed, and his household property is confiscated to give to all of you. Exert yourselves fully for the state and do not imitate this man."
translations.idiomatic: Now Baisa has been imprisoned, will never again be employed, and his household property is confiscated to give to all of you. Exert yourselves fully for the state and do not imitate this man."

sentences.zh: 囚白撒七日而餓死，發其弟承麟、子狗兒徐州安置。

translations.literal: Baisa was imprisoned seven days and starved to death; his younger brother Chenglong and his son Gou'er were sent to Xuzhou for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days in prison Baisa was starved to death. His brother Chenglong and son Gou'er were resettled in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，衛州之舉本自官奴，歸之白撒則亦過矣。

translations.literal: Commentators at the time said the Weizhou campaign had originated with Guan Nu; to lay it all on Baisa was also excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that the Weizhou campaign had begun with Guan Nu; to blame Baisa alone was likewise unjust.

sentences.zh: 初，瀕河居民聞官軍北渡，築坦塞戶，潛伏洞穴，及見官奴一軍號令明肅，撫勞周悉，所過無絲發之犯，老幼婦子坦然相視，無復畏避。

translations.literal: At first, when riverside residents heard the government army was crossing north, they built ramparts and blocked their doors and hid in caves; but when they saw Guan Nu's army with clear and strict orders, thorough comfort and labor, and not the slightest violation wherever they passed, old and young, women and children looked at one another openly without fear.
translations.idiomatic: At first, hearing the court army was crossing north, riverside folk walled their homes, barred their doors, and hid in caves. Guan Nu's command marched with strict discipline and thoughtful care; they harmed no one along the way, and old and young faced them without fear.

sentences.zh: 俄白撒輩縱軍四出，剽掠俘虜，挑掘焚炙，靡所不至。

translations.literal: Soon Baisa and his sort let the army loose in all directions—plundering, taking captives, gouging out and burning—there was nowhere they did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Baisa and his followers unleashed their troops in every direction—looting, taking captives, torturing and burning—leaving nothing untouched.

sentences.zh: 哭聲相接，屍骸盈野。

translations.literal: Wailing voices linked one to another; corpses filled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing ran without pause; the fields were heaped with corpses.

sentences.zh: 都尉高祿謙、苗用秀輩仍掠人食之，而白撒誅斬在口，所過官吏殘虐不勝，一飯之費有數十金不能給者，公私皇皇，日皆徯大兵至矣。

translations.literal: Commandants Gao Luqian, Miao Yongxiu, and their like still seized people for food; Baisa's executions and beheadings were always on his lips; officials along the route were so cruelly oppressed they could not bear it—a single meal might cost dozens of gold pieces that could not be paid; public and private were alike in panic, and each day they only awaited the great army's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Commandants Gao Luqian, Miao Yongxiu, and others seized people for food. Baisa spoke constantly of executions. Officials along the route were crushed by cruelty; a single meal might cost dozens of gold pieces none could pay. Public and private life alike trembled, each day awaiting the northern army.

sentences.zh: 白撒目不知書，奸黠有餘，簿書政事，聞之即解，善談議，多知，接人則煦煦然，好貨殖，能捭闔中人主心，遂浸漬以取將相。

translations.literal: Baisa's eyes could not read books, yet he was abundantly crafty and cunning; on documents and government affairs, once he heard them he understood; he was skilled at discussion and knew much; in receiving people he was warm and genial; he loved trade and profit and could sway and open the ruler's heart—thus by gradual soaking he attained general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa could not read, yet he was surpassingly cunning. Hear a document or policy once and he grasped it. He spoke well, knew much, and received people with warmth. He loved profit and knew how to sway the throne—by degrees he rose to general and minister.

sentences.zh: 既富貴，起第於汴之西城，規模擬宮掖，婢妾百數，皆衣金縷，奴隸月廩與列將等，猶以爲未足也。

translations.literal: Once wealthy and honored, he raised a mansion in Bian's western quarter, its scale modeled on the palace inner quarters; his maids and concubines numbered in the hundreds, all clothed in gold thread; slaves' monthly rations matched those of ranked generals—yet he still thought it insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Once rich and powerful, he built a mansion in western Bian modeled on the palace. He kept hundreds of concubines in gold-thread robes and paid his slaves monthly rations equal to a field general's—yet still wanted more.

sentences.zh: 上嘗遣中使責之曰：「卿汲汲於此，將無北歸意耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor once sent a palace envoy to reprove him, saying: "You are so eager in this—have you no intention of returning north?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent a palace envoy to rebuke him: "You are so busy with this—do you mean never to return north?"

sentences.zh: 白撒終不悛，以及於禍。

translations.literal: Baisa never repented, and thus came to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Baisa never mended his ways, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：白撒本非將才，恇怯誤國，徒能阿合以取富貴，性愎貪鄙，當此危亡，方謀封殖以自逸，此猶大廈將焚而燕雀不悟者歟！

translations.literal: The encomium says: Baisa was never a general's material—timid and cowardly, he misled the state, able only to fawn and agree to win wealth and rank; by nature obstinate, greedy, and base, at this hour of peril and ruin he still plotted to enrich himself for ease—was this not like swallows and sparrows unaware as the great hall is about to burn!
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Baisa was no soldier—timidity and cowardice misled the state. He fawned his way to wealth, obstinate, greedy, and base. At the hour of ruin he still schemed for private ease—like swallows in the eaves while the hall burns.

sentences.zh: 赤盞合喜

translations.literal: Chizhan Hexi
translations.idiomatic: Chizhan Hexi

sentences.zh: 赤盞合喜，性剛愎，好自用，朝廷以其有才幹任之。

translations.literal: Chizhan Hexi was stubborn by nature and liked to follow his own views, but the court appointed him because he had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhan Hexi was stubborn by nature and liked to follow his own views, but the court appointed him because he had talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，累遷蘭州刺史、提控軍馬。

translations.literal: In Xuanzong's time, he rose through successive promotions to prefect of Lanzhou and controller of military forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's time, he rose through successive promotions to prefect of Lanzhou and controller of military forces.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年十一月，夏人四萬餘騎圍定西，輦致攻具，將取其城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, more than forty thousand Xia cavalry surrounded Dingxi and brought up siege equipment by cart, intending to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, more than forty thousand Xia cavalry surrounded Dingxi and brought up siege equipment by cart, intending to take the city.

sentences.zh: 合喜及楊斡烈等率兵鏖戰走之，斬首二千級，俘數十人，獲馬八百餘匹，器械稱是，餘悉遁去。

translations.literal: Hexi, Yang Wolie, and the others led troops in fierce battle and drove them off, cutting off two thousand heads, capturing several dozen men, taking more than eight hundred horses and a comparable number of weapons, while the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi, Yang Wolie, and the others led troops in fierce battle and drove them off, cutting off two thousand heads, capturing several dozen men, taking more than eight hundred horses and a comparable number of weapons, while the rest all fled.

sentences.zh: 興定元年正月，以屢敗夏人，遙授同知臨洮府事，兼前職。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingding, because he had repeatedly defeated the Xia, he was remotely appointed vice prefect of Lintao while retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Xingding, because he had repeatedly defeated the Xia, he was remotely appointed vice prefect of Lintao while retaining his former post.

sentences.zh: 是冬，陝西行省奉詔伐宋，合喜權行元帥府，駐來遠寨以張聲勢，既而獲捷。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat received an edict to campaign against the Song, Hexi temporarily administered the Marshal's Office and stationed at Laiyuan Fort to make a show of force; soon he won a victory.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat received an edict to campaign against the Song, Hexi temporarily administered the Marshal's Office and stationed at Laiyuan Fort to make a show of force; soon he won a victory.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，宋兵數千侵臨洮，合喜擊走之，斬獲甚衆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, several thousand Song troops invaded Lintao. Hexi attacked and drove them off, killing and capturing very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year, several thousand Song troops invaded Lintao. Hexi attacked and drove them off, killing and capturing very many.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，遷元帥左都監，行元帥府事于鞏州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, he was promoted to left supervisor-in-chief of the Marshalate and administered the Marshal's Office at Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, he was promoted to left supervisor-in-chief of the Marshalate and administered the Marshal's Office at Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，夏人犯邊，合喜討之，師次鹿兒原，遇復兵千人，遣提控烏古論世顯率偏師敗之，都統王定亦破其衆一千五百於新泉城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, Xia troops violated the border; Hexi campaigned against them. The army halted at Deer-Child Plain, met a thousand Xia relief troops, and sent Commander Wugulun Shixian with a detached force to defeat them; Commander-in-Chief Wang Ding also broke fifteen hundred of their men at Xinquan City.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, fourth month, the Xia raided the frontier and Hexi marched against them. At Deer-Child Plain he met a thousand Xia reinforcements and sent Commander Wugulun Shixian with a flanking force to rout them; Commander-in-Chief Wang Ding destroyed another fifteen hundred at Xinquan.

sentences.zh: 九月，夏人攻鞏州，合喜遣兵擊之，一日十余戰，夏人退據南閑，遣精兵三萬傅城，又擊走之，生擒夏將劉打、甲玉等。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Xia attacked Gongzhou; Hexi sent troops to strike them—more than ten battles in a single day. The Xia fell back and held South Pass, sent thirty thousand elite troops to press the walls, and were again driven off; the Xia generals Liu Da, Jia Yu, and others were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Xia attacked Gongzhou. Hexi met them in more than ten battles in one day. The Xia withdrew to South Pass and sent thirty thousand elite troops against the walls; he drove them off again and took the Xia generals Liu Da and Jia Yu alive.

sentences.zh: 訊知夏大將你思丁、兀名二人謀，以爲鞏帥府所在，鞏既下則臨洮、積石、河、洮諸城不攻自破，故先及鞏，且構宋統制程信等將兵四萬來攻。

translations.literal: On interrogation it was learned that the Xia great generals Nisiding and Wuming had plotted that, since the Gong commandery headquarters lay there, once Gong fell the cities of Lintao, Jishi, He, Tao, and the rest would collapse without attack—hence they had struck Gong first—and had moreover incited Song Commander Cheng Xin and others to bring forty thousand troops in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation revealed that Xia generals Nisiding and Wuming had planned to take Gong first—the commandery seat—so that Lintao, Jishi, He, Tao, and the rest would fall without a fight. They had also enlisted Song Commander Cheng Xin with forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 合喜聞之，飭兵嚴備。

translations.literal: When Hexi heard this he disciplined the troops and made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi heard this and tightened discipline and defenses.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵果至，合喜督兵搏戰，卻之，殺數千人。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy army indeed arrived; Hexi directed the troops in close combat, drove them back, and killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon arrived. Hexi led the fight in person, drove them back, and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 攻益急，將士殊死戰，殺傷者以萬計。

translations.literal: The assault grew fiercer; officers and soldiers fought to the death; the killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The assault intensified. Officers and men fought to the death; casualties on both sides ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 夏人焚其攻具，拔柵而去。

translations.literal: The Xia burned their siege equipment, uprooted their palisades, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia burned their siege gear, pulled up their stockades, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 合喜已先伏甲要地邀之，復率衆躡其後，斬首甚衆。

translations.literal: Hexi had already hidden armor in key places to intercept them; he again led the host in pursuit from behind and beheaded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi had already posted troops at key points to ambush them, then pursued and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 十月，以功遙授平西軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, for his merit he was remotely appointed Military Commissioner of the Pingxi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Pingxi Army in absentia for his service.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，大將萌古不花攻鳳翔，朝廷以主將完顏仲元孤軍不足守禦，命合喜將兵援之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang the great general Menggubuhua attacked Fengxiang; the court, because the commanding general Wanyan Zhongyuan's isolated army was insufficient for defense, ordered Hexi to lead troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang the great general Menggubuhua attacked Fengxiang. The court judged Commander Wanyan Zhongyuan's isolated force too weak to hold the city and ordered Hexi to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，木華黎國王、斜里吉不花等及夏人步騎數十萬圍鳳翔，東自扶風、岐山，西連汧、隴，數百里間皆其營柵，攻城甚急，合喜盡力，僅能禦之。

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, King Muqali, Xielijibuhua, and others together with Xia foot and horse in the hundreds of thousands besieged Fengxiang; east from Fufeng and Qishan, west linking Qian and Long, for several hundred li all were their camps and palisades; the assault on the city was very urgent—Hexi exerted all his strength and could barely hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, second month, King Muqali, Xielijibuhua, and others with hundreds of thousands of Xia foot and horse besieged Fengxiang. From Fufeng and Qishan in the east to Qian and Long in the west, their camps stretched hundreds of li. The assault was fierce; Hexi strained every resource and barely held.

sentences.zh: 於是，合喜以同知臨洮府事顏盞蝦蟆戰尤力，遂以便宜升爲通遠軍節度使，上嘉其功，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hexi, because Associate Administrator of Lintao Prefecture Yanzhan Xiami had fought with especial force, promoted him on discretionary authority to Military Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army; the emperor praised his merit and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi noted that Lintao Associate Administrator Yanzhan Xiami had fought with exceptional valor and promoted him on his own authority to Military Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲，升簽樞密院事。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted to Privy Council Signatory.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made Privy Council Signatory.

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，拜參知政事，權樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong took the throne, Hexi was appointed Participation Councillor and Acting Deputy Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong ascended the throne, Hexi was appointed Participation Councillor and Acting Deputy Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 正大八年十一月，鄧州馳報大元兵破嶢峰關，由金州東下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year of Zhengda, Dengzhou sent urgent word that Great Yuan troops had broken Yaofeng Pass and were marching east down from Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhengda 8, Dengzhou sent urgent word that Great Yuan forces had broken Yaofeng Pass and were marching east from Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 報至時日已暮，省院官入奏，上曰：「事至於此，奈何？」

translations.literal: When the report arrived the day was already dusk; provincial and court officials entered to memorialize; the emperor said: "Matters have come to this—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The report arrived at dusk. Provincial and court officials memorialized. The emperor said, "Matters have come to this—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 上即位至是八年，從在東宮日立十三都尉，每尉不下萬人，強壯矯捷，極爲精練。

translations.literal: From his accession to this point was eight years; while still in the Eastern Palace he had established thirteen commandant offices, each with no fewer than ten thousand men, strong, sturdy, and nimble, drilled to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned eight years. As heir apparent he had raised thirteen commandant commands of no fewer than ten thousand men each—hardy, agile, and drilled to a fine edge.

sentences.zh: 步卒負擔器甲糧糗重至六七斗，一日夜行二百里。

translations.literal: Foot soldiers bore weapons, armor, and rations weighing as much as six or seven dou, and in one day and night marched two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Foot soldiers carried arms, armor, and rations of six or seven dou and could march two hundred li in a day and night.

sentences.zh: 忠孝軍萬八千人，皆回紇、河西及中州人夜掠而逃歸者，人有從馬，以騎射選之乃得補。

translations.literal: The Zhongxiao Army of eighteen thousand were all Uighurs, Hexi men, and Central Plain people who had raided by night and fled back; a man had to have a follower horse and be chosen by mounted archery before he could be enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: The eighteen-thousand-man Zhongxiao Army drew on Uighurs, Hexi men, and Central Plain raiders who had fled back by night. A man needed his own mount and had to pass a mounted-archery test to enlist.

sentences.zh: 親衛、騎兵、武衛、護衛，遷外諸軍又二十余萬。

translations.literal: Personal Guards, cavalry, Martial Guards, and Imperial Guards, together with transferred external armies, came to another two hundred thousand and more.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Guards, cavalry, Martial Guards, Imperial Guards, and transferred frontier armies added another two hundred thousand and more.

sentences.zh: 故頻年有大昌原、倒回穀之捷，士氣既振，遂有一戰之資。

translations.literal: Thus in successive years there had been victories at Dachangyuan and Daohuigu; morale had been roused, and there was now the means for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years victories at Dachangyuan and Daohuigu had raised morale; the court still had strength for one great fight.

sentences.zh: 至是，院官同奏：「北軍冒萬里之險，曆二年之久，方入武休，其勞苦已極。

translations.literal: At this point the court officials jointly memorialized: "The northern army has braved ten thousand li of peril and passed two years before entering Wuxiu—their toil and hardship are already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials jointly memorialized: "The northern army has braved ten thousand li and two years' march to reach Wuxiu—they are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 爲吾計者，以兵屯睢、鄭、昌武、歸德及京畿諸縣，以大將守洛陽、潼關、懷、孟等處，嚴兵備之。

translations.literal: Our plan should be to station troops at Sui, Zheng, Changwu, Guide, and the capital districts, place great generals to hold Luoyang, Tong Pass, Huai, Meng, and other places, and make strict military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Our plan: garrison Sui, Zheng, Changwu, Guide, and the capital districts; post great generals at Luoyang, Tong Pass, Huai, Meng, and the like; and hold every line in strength.

sentences.zh: 京師積糧數百萬斛，令河南州郡堅壁清野，百姓不能入城者聚保山砦。

translations.literal: The capital has stored grain in the millions of hu; order the Henan prefectures and commanderies to strengthen walls and clear the countryside; common people who cannot enter the cities should gather and defend mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The capital holds millions of hu of grain. Order Henan commanderies to strengthen walls and clear the countryside; those who cannot reach the cities should hold mountain stockades.

sentences.zh: 彼深入之師，欲攻不能，欲戰不得，師老食盡，不擊自歸矣。」

translations.literal: That deeply penetrating army will wish to attack but cannot, wish to fight but may not; when the army is weary and food exhausted, without striking they will return of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Their deep column will neither take a city nor win a battle. When their troops are spent and their grain gone, they will withdraw without our striking a blow."

sentences.zh: 上太息曰：「南渡二十年，所在之民破田宅、鬻妻子以養軍士。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "Twenty years since the southern crossing—the people everywhere have ruined fields and houses and sold wives and children to feed the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed. "Twenty years since the southern crossing, the people have ruined their fields and homes and sold wives and children to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 且諸軍無慮二十余萬，今敵至不能迎戰，徒以自保，京城雖存，何以爲國，天下其謂我何！」

translations.literal: Moreover the armies are no less than two hundred thousand and more—now that the enemy has come we cannot meet them in battle and only seek to preserve ourselves; though the capital may survive, how can this be a state—what will the realm say of me!"
translations.idiomatic: We have two hundred thousand troops. The enemy is here and we will not fight—only hide behind walls. If the capital survives but we will not battle, what kind of state is this? What will the realm say of me!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「存亡 天命，惟不負民可也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Survival or ruin rests with Heaven's mandate—only not failing the people is possible."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Survival or ruin is Heaven's will—but we must not fail our people."

sentences.zh: 乃詔合達、蒲阿等屯軍襄、鄧。

translations.literal: He then ordered Wanyan Hedda, Pusan A, and others to station troops at Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Wanyan Hedda, Pusan A, and others to encamp at Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，兩省軍潰於三峰山，北兵進薄京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year the armies of the two departments were routed at Sanfeng Mountain; the northern troops pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year the combined armies were routed at Sanfeng Mountain, and northern forces closed on the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，議曹王出質。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the third month they debated sending Prince Cao as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the third month the court debated sending Prince Cao as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 大兵北行，留速不泬攻城，攻具已辦，既有納質之請，即又云：「有我受命攻城，但曹王出則退，不然不罷也。」

translations.literal: The great army marched north, leaving Subutai to besiege the city; siege equipment was already prepared. Though there was a request to send a hostage, they then also said: "I have received orders to attack the city—only if Prince Cao comes out will we withdraw; otherwise we will not cease."
translations.idiomatic: The main army marched north, leaving Subutai to besiege the city with siege gear already in place. Though the court sought to send a hostage, they said: "I have orders to take the city—withdraw only if Prince Cao is delivered; otherwise we will not stop."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，曹王入辭，宴于宮中。

translations.literal: On renyin Prince Cao entered to take leave; a banquet was held in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Prince Cao came to bid farewell, and the court feasted him in the palace.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，北兵立攻具，沿壕列木柵，以薪草填壕，頃刻平十余步。

translations.literal: On guimao the northern troops set up siege equipment, lined wooden palisades along the moat, and filled the moat with firewood and grass—in a moment they leveled more than ten paces.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the northerners raised siege engines, lined the moat with wooden palisades, and filled it with brush—in moments they leveled more than ten paces.

sentences.zh: 主兵者以議和之故不敢與戰，但於城上坐視而已。

translations.literal: The commanders of troops, because peace talks were under way, dared not give battle and only sat on the walls watching.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders, fearing to spoil the peace talks, dared not fight and only watched from the walls.

sentences.zh: 城中喧哄，上聞之，從六七騎出端門至舟橋。

translations.literal: Uproar rose within the city; when the emperor heard it he rode out with six or seven horsemen from Duangate to the Boat Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Uproar filled the city. Hearing it, the emperor rode out with six or seven men from Duangate to the Boat Bridge.

sentences.zh: 時新雨淖，車駕忽出，人驚愕失措，但跪於道傍，亦有望而拜者，上自麾之曰：「勿拜，恐泥汙汝衣。」

translations.literal: Fresh rain had made the ground mire; the imperial carriage suddenly appeared and people were startled beyond composure—they only knelt by the roadside, and some who saw from afar also bowed; the emperor himself waved them off, saying: "Do not bow—you will muddy your clothes."
translations.idiomatic: Fresh rain had turned the streets to mire. The imperial procession appeared without warning; people froze and knelt along the road, and some in the distance bowed as well. The emperor waved them off: "Do not bow—you will foul your clothes."

sentences.zh: 倉皇中，市肆米豆狼藉於地，上敕衛士令各歸其家，老幼遮擁至有誤觸御衣者。

translations.literal: In the confusion grain and beans from market stalls lay scattered on the ground; the emperor ordered the guards to tell each to return home; old and young pressed about him until some accidentally touched the imperial robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the confusion rice and beans lay scattered in the markets. He ordered the guards to send people home. Old and young pressed so close that some brushed his robe.

sentences.zh: 少頃，宰相從官皆至，進笠不受，曰：「軍士暴露，我何用此爲。」

translations.literal: Before long the chief ministers and attendant officials all arrived; they offered bamboo hats but he would not take them, saying: "The soldiers stand exposed—what use have I for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the chief ministers and attendants arrived. They offered bamboo hats, but he refused: "The soldiers stand in the open—what need have I of shelter?"

sentences.zh: 所過慰勞軍士，皆踴躍稱萬歲，臣等戰死無所恨，至有感泣者。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he comforted and encouraged the soldiers; all leapt up shouting "Long live the emperor!" "We ministers would die in battle without regret"—some were moved even to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he comforted the troops. They leapt up shouting "Long live the emperor!" "We would die without regret"—some wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 西南軍士五六十輩聚而若有言者，上就問之，跪曰：「大兵芻土填壕，功已過半，平章傳令勿放一鏃，恐壞和事，想豈有計耶？」

translations.literal: Fifty or sixty soldiers of the southwest sector gathered as if they had something to say; the emperor went up and questioned them; kneeling, they said: "The great army is filling the moat with straw and earth—the work is already more than half done; the participation councillor has transmitted orders not to loose a single arrow, fearing to ruin the peace talks—can there be any plan at all?"
translations.idiomatic: Fifty or sixty soldiers from the southwest corner gathered as if to speak. The emperor asked them. Kneeling, they said: "The enemy is half-filling the moat with earth and straw, yet the participation councillor forbids a single arrow for fear of spoiling peace—have you any plan?"

sentences.zh: 上顧謂其中長者云：「朕爲生靈，稱臣進奉無不從順，止有一子，養來成長，今往作質子矣。

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said to the eldest among them: "I act for the living people—in submitting as vassal and sending tribute I have refused nothing; I have only one son, raised to manhood, who now goes to serve as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to their elder. "I have done everything for the people—submitted, paid tribute, withheld nothing. I have one son, raised to manhood, who now goes as hostage.

sentences.zh: 汝等略忍，待曹王出，大兵不退，汝等死戰未晚。」

translations.literal: Bear with it a little; wait until Prince Cao goes out—if the great army does not withdraw, it will not be too late for you to fight to the death."
translations.idiomatic: Bear with it a little longer. When Prince Cao is sent out, if the enemy still does not withdraw, then fight to the death—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 復有拜泣者曰：「事急矣，聖主毋望和事。」

translations.literal: Again someone bowed and wept, saying: "The matter is urgent—Your Majesty must not hope for peace."
translations.idiomatic: Another man bowed, weeping: "The crisis is upon us—Your Majesty must abandon hope of peace."

sentences.zh: 乃傳旨城上放箭。

translations.literal: He then transmitted an order for the walls to loose arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the defenders to shoot.

sentences.zh: 西水門千戶劉壽控御馬仰視曰：「聖主無信賊臣，賊臣盡，大兵退矣。」

translations.literal: Liu Shou, chiliarch of the West Water Gate, reined in his horse, looked up, and said: "Your Majesty must not trust traitorous ministers—when the traitorous ministers are gone, the great army will withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shou, chiliarch of the West Water Gate, reined in his horse and cried up: "Your Majesty must not trust traitors—drive them out and the enemy will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 衛士欲擊之，上止曰：「醉矣，勿問。」

translations.literal: The guards wished to strike him; the emperor stopped them, saying: "He is drunk—do not trouble him."
translations.idiomatic: The guards moved to seize him. The emperor said, "He is drunk—leave him be."

sentences.zh: 是日，曹王出詣軍前，大兵並力進攻。

translations.literal: That day Prince Cao went out to the enemy camp; the great army pressed the assault with combined force.
translations.idiomatic: That day Prince Cao went out to the enemy camp, and the northerners redoubled the assault.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上復出撫東門將士，太學生楊奐等前白事。

translations.literal: On jiachen the emperor again went out to comfort the officers and soldiers at the East Gate; Imperial University students Yang Huan and others came forward to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the emperor again went out to encourage the troops at the East Gate. Imperial University students Yang Huan and others came forward to petition.

sentences.zh: 上問何所欲言，曰：「臣等皆太學生，令執砲夫之役，恐非國家百年以來待士之意。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked what they wished to say; they said: "We are all Imperial University students; to be ordered to serve as catapult crews—this is perhaps not the state's intent in treating scholars these hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: He asked what they wished to say. They replied: "We are Imperial University students. To be made catapult crews is hardly how the state has treated scholars these hundred years."

sentences.zh: 敕記姓名，即免其役。

translations.literal: He ordered their names recorded and at once exempted them from the duty.
translations.idiomatic: He had their names recorded and at once released them from duty.

sentences.zh: 過南薰門，值被創者，親傅以藥，手酌卮酒以賜，且出內府金帛以待有功者。

translations.literal: Passing the South Fragrance Gate he met the wounded, personally applied medicine, with his own hand poured cup wine to bestow, and also brought out inner-palace gold and silks to await those with merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the South Fragrance Gate he came upon the wounded, dressed their wounds himself, poured wine with his own hand, and brought out palace gold and silks to reward the valiant.

sentences.zh: 是日，大兵驅漢俘及婦女老幼負薪草填壕塹，城上箭鏃四下如雨，頃刻壕爲之平。

translations.literal: That day the great army drove Han captives and women, old and young, to carry firewood and grass and fill the moat and trenches; arrowheads from the walls fell on all sides like rain—in a moment the moat was leveled.
translations.idiomatic: That day the enemy drove Han captives and civilians—women, old, and young—to fill the moat with brush. Arrows fell from the walls like rain, yet in moments the moat was level.

sentences.zh: 龍德宮造砲石，取宋太湖、靈璧假山爲之，小大各有斤重，其圓如燈球之狀，有不如度者杖其工人。

translations.literal: Longde Palace made catapult stones, taking Song Taihu and Lingbi garden rocks for the purpose; large and small each had its weight in jin; they were round like lantern-globes in shape; workers not meeting the standard were beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Longde Palace cast catapult stones from Song garden rocks of Taihu and Lingbi, each weighed to specification and shaped like lantern globes. Workers who missed the standard were beaten.

sentences.zh: 大兵用砲則不然，破大磑或碌碡爲二三，皆用之。

translations.literal: The great army's use of catapults was not so: they broke great millstones or stone rollers into two or three pieces and all were used.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did otherwise: they shattered millstones and rollers into pieces and hurled them all.

sentences.zh: 攢竹砲有至十三稍者，餘砲稱是。

translations.literal: Bundled-bamboo catapults had some reaching thirteen arms; the rest of the artillery matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Their bundled-bamboo trebuchets had as many as thirteen arms; the rest of their artillery matched.

sentences.zh: 每城一角置砲百餘枝，更遞下上，晝夜不息，不數日，石幾與裏城平。

translations.literal: At each corner of the city they placed more than a hundred catapults, relieving one another up and down, day and night without cease; in not many days the stones nearly reached level with the inner wall.
translations.idiomatic: At each corner they posted more than a hundred engines, relieved in shifts day and night. Within days the stone heaps nearly reached the inner wall.

sentences.zh: 而城上樓櫓皆故宮及芳華、玉溪所拆大木爲之，合抱之木，隨擊而碎，以馬糞麥秸布其上，綱索旃褥固護之。

translations.literal: Yet the towers and parapets on the walls were all made of great timbers dismantled from the old palace and from Fanghua and Yuxi; timbers one could embrace were shattered with each strike; horse dung and wheat straw were spread atop them, and ropes, felt, and quilts were used to bind and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: The wall towers were built of great timbers stripped from the old palace and from Fanghua and Yuxi. Timbers thick as a man's embrace splintered under each blow. The defenders spread horse dung and straw atop them and bound them with rope, felt, and quilts.

sentences.zh: 其懸風板之外皆以牛皮爲障，遂謂不可近。

translations.literal: Outside the hanging wind-boards oxhide was used entirely as screens, and thus they deemed the enemy could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the hanging wind-shields they hung oxhide screens and believed the enemy could not come near.

sentences.zh: 大兵以火砲擊之，隨即延爇不可撲救。

translations.literal: The great army struck them with fire-cannons; at once the blaze spread and could not be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy hurled fire bombs; the flames spread at once and nothing could put them out.

sentences.zh: 父老所傳周世宗築京城，取虎牢土爲之，堅密如鐵，受砲所擊唯凹而已。

translations.literal: Elders transmit that when Emperor Shizong of Zhou built the capital walls, he took earth from Hulao to make them, dense and hard as iron; struck by catapult-shot they only dented.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that Emperor Shizong of Zhou had built the walls with earth from Hulao, hard as iron, so that cannon-stones only dented them.

sentences.zh: 大兵壕外築城圍百五十里，城有乳口樓櫓，壕深丈許，闊亦如之，約三四十步置一鋪，鋪置百許人守之。

translations.literal: Outside the moat the great army built an encircling wall one hundred fifty li around; the wall had embrasures and towers; the moat was more than a zhang deep and as wide; roughly every thirty or forty paces they placed a post-station, each post-station with about a hundred men to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the moat the enemy threw up a circumvallation one hundred fifty li around, with embrasures and watchtowers. The moat was over a zhang deep and as wide. Every thirty or forty paces they set a guard post with roughly a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 初，白撒命築門外短牆，委曲狹隘容二三人得過，以防大兵奪門。

translations.literal: At first Baisa ordered short walls built outside the gates, winding and narrow so only two or three men could pass, to guard against the great army seizing the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wanyan Baisa had ordered low walls built outside each gate, twisting and narrow enough for only two or three men abreast, lest the enemy rush the gates.

sentences.zh: 及被攻，諸將請乘夜斫營，軍乃不能猝出，比出，已爲北兵所覺。

translations.literal: When attack came, the generals asked to raid camp by night; the army could not burst out suddenly; by the time they emerged, the northern troops had already detected them.
translations.idiomatic: Under assault the generals proposed a night raid, but the troops could not pour out at once; by the time they did, the northerners had been alerted.

sentences.zh: 後又夜募死士千人，穴城由壕徑渡，燒其砲坐。

translations.literal: Later they again recruited a thousand death-defying men by night, tunneled through the wall and crossed the moat directly, and burned their artillery platforms.
translations.idiomatic: They then raised a thousand volunteers by night, tunneled through the wall, crossed the moat, and torched the enemy's gun emplacements.

sentences.zh: 城上懸紅紙燈爲應，約燈起渡壕，又爲圍者所覺。

translations.literal: On the wall they hung red paper lamps as signals, agreeing that when the lamps rose they would cross the moat; again the besiegers detected them.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders hung red paper lanterns on the wall as signals to cross when they were raised—again the besiegers saw through it.

sentences.zh: 又放紙鳶，置文書其上，至北營則斷之，以誘被俘者。

translations.literal: They also released paper kites, placed documents on them, and when they reached the northern camp cut them loose, to lure captured men.
translations.idiomatic: They also flew paper kites with messages; when a kite reached the northern camp they severed the line, hoping to lure captives with false intelligence.

sentences.zh: 識者謂前日紙燈、今日紙鳶，宰相以此退敵難矣。

translations.literal: Observers said: yesterday paper lamps, today paper kites—the chief minister expects to drive off the enemy with such means; this will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Observers remarked that paper lanterns one day and kites the next would hardly drive off an army—the chief minister's stratagems had come to this.

sentences.zh: 右丞世魯命作《江水曲》，使城上之人靜夜唱之，蓋河朔先有此曲以寄謳吟之思，其謬計如此。

translations.literal: Right Vice Councillor Yan Shilu ordered the composition of "River Water Song" and had those on the wall sing it on quiet nights—probably because north of the river this tune already existed to carry thoughts of lament; their mistaken plans went so far.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Councillor Yan Shilu had a "River Water Song" composed and ordered the wall-guards to sing it on still nights—a tune from Hebei already used for homesick longing. Such were their counsels.

sentences.zh: 合喜先以守鳳翔自誇，及令守西北隅，其地受攻最急，而合喜當之，語言失措，面無人色。

translations.literal: Hexi had first boasted of holding Fengxiang; when ordered to hold the northwest corner, that sector bore the fiercest assault, and Hexi faced it—his words went awry and his face was without human color.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhan Hexi had once boasted of his defense of Fengxiang; now assigned the northwest corner, where the assault was fiercest, he lost his composure and his face went ashen.

sentences.zh: 軍士特以車駕數出慰勞，人自激昂，爭爲效命耳。

translations.literal: The soldiers relied solely on the imperial carriage coming out several times to comfort them; each man roused himself and vied to offer his life.
translations.idiomatic: The troops fought on because the emperor rode out again and again to encourage them—each man found his own zeal and vied to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 其守城之具有火砲名「震天雷」者，鐵罐盛藥，以火點之，砲起火發，其聲如雷，聞百里外，所爇圍半畝之上，火點著甲鐵皆透。

translations.literal: Among the city-defense devices was a fire-cannon named "Heaven-Shaking Thunder": an iron jar holding powder, ignited by fire; the cannon's fire erupted, its sound like thunder, heard a hundred li away; what it burned covered more than half an acre; fire-points penetrated even armor and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Their arsenal included a bomb called "Heaven-Shaking Thunder"—powder in an iron pot, touched off by flame. It detonated like thunder, audible a hundred li away, scorched half an acre, and burned through armor and iron.

sentences.zh: 大兵又爲牛皮洞，直至城下，掘城爲龕，間可容人，則城上不可奈何矣。

translations.literal: The great army also made oxhide tunnels reaching right to the foot of the wall, dug the wall into niches with room enough at intervals for a man, and then those on the wall could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy drove oxhide-covered saps to the wall, dug niches large enough for a man, and left the defenders helpless above.

sentences.zh: 人有獻策者，以鐵繩懸「震天雷」者，順城而下，至掘處火發，人與牛皮皆碎迸無跡。

translations.literal: Someone proposed using iron chains to lower "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" along the wall; when it reached the digging place and the fire went off, men and oxhide were all smashed and scattered without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Someone proposed using iron chains to lower "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" along the wall; when it reached the digging place and the fire went off, men and oxhide were all smashed and scattered without trace.

sentences.zh: 又飛火槍，注藥以火發之，輒前燒十余步，人亦不敢近。

translations.literal: There were also flying fire-lances; powder was poured in and ignited by fire; they at once burned more than ten paces ahead and no one dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: They also used fire-lances—powder packed and ignited, the flame racing ten paces forward so that no one dared come near.

sentences.zh: 大兵惟畏此二物云。

translations.literal: The great army feared only these two things, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, it was said, feared only these two weapons.

sentences.zh: 四月罷攻。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the assault was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 至是十六晝夜矣，內外死者以百萬計，大兵知不可下，乃謾爲好語云：「兩國已講和，更相攻耶？」

translations.literal: By this point sixteen days and nights had passed, and the dead inside and outside were counted in the hundreds of thousands. The great army knew the city could not be taken and therefore deceitfully made conciliatory words, saying, "The two states have already negotiated peace. Why attack each other further?"
translations.idiomatic: By this point sixteen days and nights had passed, and the dead inside and outside were counted in the hundreds of thousands. The great army knew the city could not be taken and therefore deceitfully made conciliatory words, saying, "The two states have already negotiated peace. Why attack each other further?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦就應之。

translations.literal: And the court in turn responded accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The court pretended to believe them.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣戶部侍郎楊居仁出宜秋門以酒炙犒師，於是營幕稍稍外遷，遂退兵。

translations.literal: Next day they sent Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Juren out through the Yiqu Autumn Gate with wine and roasted meat to reward the army; then the camp sheds slowly moved outward and at last they withdrew troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Vice Minister Yang Juren went out through the Yiqu Autumn Gate with wine and roast meat to feast the troops. The encampment gradually shifted away and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，合喜以大兵退，議入賀。

translations.literal: On renxu, because the great army withdrew, Hexi discussed entering to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, with the enemy gone, Hexi proposed a court celebration.

sentences.zh: 諸相皆不欲，獨合喜以守城爲己功，持論甚力，呼令史元好問曰：「罷攻已三日而不入賀，何也？

translations.literal: All the chief ministers were unwilling; only Hexi, taking the defense of the city as his own merit, pressed the argument very hard, and called the clerk Yuan Haowen, saying: "The assault has been lifted three days and you still do not enter to congratulate—why?
translations.idiomatic: The other ministers refused; Hexi alone claimed the defense as his triumph and pressed relentlessly. He summoned Clerk Yuan Haowen: "Three days since the siege lifted and still no congratulations—why?

sentences.zh: 速召翰苑官作表。」

translations.literal: Quickly summon the Hanlin Academy officials to draft the memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Quickly summon the Hanlin Academy officials to draft the memorial."

sentences.zh: 好問以白諸相，權參政內族思烈曰：「城下之盟，諸侯以爲恥，況以罷攻爲可賀歟？」

translations.literal: Haowen reported this to the chancellors. Acting Councillor Silie of the imperial clan said, "A treaty under the city walls is considered a disgrace by the feudal lords; how much more can stopping an attack be something to congratulate?"
translations.idiomatic: Haowen reported this to the chancellors. Acting Councillor Silie of the imperial clan said, "A treaty under the city walls is considered a disgrace by the feudal lords; how much more can stopping an attack be something to congratulate?"

sentences.zh: 合喜怒曰：「社稷不亡，帝后免難，汝等不以爲喜耶？」

translations.literal: Hexi was angry and said, "The altars of soil and grain have not perished, and the emperor and empress have escaped disaster. Do you not consider this a joy?"
translations.idiomatic: Hexi was angry and said, "The altars of soil and grain have not perished, and the emperor and empress have escaped disaster. Do you not consider this a joy?"

sentences.zh: 明日，近侍局直長張天任至省，好問私以賀議告之，天任曰：「人不知恥乃若是耶！」

translations.literal: The next day, Zhang Tianren, bureau director of the Palace Attendants, came to the Department. Haowen privately told him of the congratulation proposal, and Tianren said, "Can people fail to know shame to this degree?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day, Zhang Tianren, bureau director of the Palace Attendants, came to the Department. Haowen privately told him of the congratulation proposal, and Tianren said, "Can people fail to know shame to this degree?"

sentences.zh: 因謂諸相曰：「京城受兵，上深以爲辱。

translations.literal: He then said to the chief ministers: "The capital has suffered siege—the emperor counts it a deep humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke to the ministers: "The emperor is deeply shamed that the capital was besieged.

sentences.zh: 聞百官欲入賀，誠有此否？」

translations.literal: I have heard that the hundred officials wish to enter and offer congratulations. Is this truly so?"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the hundred officials wish to enter and offer congratulations. Is this truly so?"

sentences.zh: 會學士趙秉文不肯撰表，議遂寢。

translations.literal: Just then Academician Zhao Bingwen refused to draft the memorial and the proposal therefore lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen refused to draft the memorial, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 是月，以尚書省兼樞密院事，合喜罷樞密。

translations.literal: That month Hexi was removed from the Privy Council and given concurrent charge of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That month Hexi was stripped of the Privy Council and put in charge of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 合喜既失兵柄，意殊不樂，欲銷院印，諸相謂院事仍在，印有用時，不宜毀。

translations.literal: Hexi having lost military authority was very displeased and wished to destroy the Council seal; the chief ministers said Council affairs continued and the seal would be needed—it should not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Bereft of military power, Hexi grew sullen and tried to destroy the Council's seal. The ministers said the Council still functioned and the seal would be needed again—it must not be broken.

sentences.zh: 合喜怒，欲笞其掾。

translations.literal: Hexi grew angry and wished to beat his clerks with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi raged and threatened to flog his clerks.

sentences.zh: 有投匿名書于御路云：「副樞合喜、總帥撒合、參政訛出皆國賊，朝廷不殺，衆軍亦須殺之，爲國除害。」

translations.literal: Someone threw an anonymous letter onto the imperial road, saying, "Deputy commissioner Hexi, commander-in-chief Sahe, and councillor Echu are all state traitors. If the court does not kill them, the armies must kill them and remove harm for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Someone threw an anonymous letter onto the imperial road, saying, "Deputy commissioner Hexi, commander-in-chief Sahe, and councillor Echu are all state traitors. If the court does not kill them, the armies must kill them and remove harm for the state."

sentences.zh: 衛士以聞。

translations.literal: The guards reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The guard reported it upward.

sentences.zh: 撒合飲藥死，訛出稱疾不出，惟合喜坦然若無事者，上亦無所問，由是軍國之事盡決於合喜矣。

translations.literal: Sahe took poison and died; Echu claimed illness and did not appear; only Hexi was at ease as if nothing had happened, and the emperor also made no inquiry—thereby military and state affairs were all decided by Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Sahe drank poison and died; Echu feigned illness and stayed away; Hexi alone acted unmoved, and the emperor asked nothing—henceforth Hexi decided all military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，大兵圍汴，司諫陳岢屢上封事言得失，切中時病。

translations.literal: At first, when the great army besieged Bian, Remonstrator Chen Ke repeatedly submitted sealed memorials on gains and losses, striking squarely at the ailments of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy first besieged Bian, Remonstrator Chen Ke sent repeated sealed memorials on policy, hitting the court's failures squarely.

sentences.zh: 合喜大怒，召入省，呼其名責之曰：「子爲'陳山可'耶？

translations.literal: Hexi was greatly enraged, summoned him into the Department, called his name and reproved him: "Are you 'Chen Shan-ke'?
translations.idiomatic: Hexi flew into a rage, had him brought to the Department, and shouted: "So you are 'Chen Shan-ke'?

sentences.zh: 果如子言，能退大敵，我當世世與若爲奴。」

translations.literal: If it is truly as you say and you can drive back the great enemy, I will be your slave generation after generation."
translations.idiomatic: If it is truly as you say and you can drive back the great enemy, I will be your slave generation after generation."

sentences.zh: 聞者無不竊笑。

translations.literal: Hearers all snickered in private.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard it stifled a laugh.

sentences.zh: 蓋不識「岢」字，至分爲兩耳。

translations.literal: This was because he did not recognize the character "ke" and even divided it into two parts.
translations.idiomatic: This was because he did not recognize the character "ke" and even divided it into two parts.

sentences.zh: 天興元年七月，權參知政事思烈、恆山公武仙合軍自汝州入援，詔以合喜爲樞密使，統京城軍萬五千應之，且命賽不爲之助。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianxing, Acting Participation Councillor Si Lie and Prince of Hengshan Wu Xian united armies from Ruzhou to enter as reinforcement; an edict made Hexi Privy Councilor, commanding fifteen thousand capital troops to respond, and also ordered Saibu to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 1, seventh month, Si Lie and Prince Wu Xian of Hengshan marched from Ruzhou to relieve the capital. Hexi was named Privy Councilor to lead fifteen thousand city troops to meet them, with Wanyan Saibu ordered to aid him.

sentences.zh: 八月己酉朔，駐於近郊，候益兵乃進屯中牟古城。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, jiayou, they encamped in the near suburbs, waited for reinforcements to increase, then advanced and encamped at the old city of Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the eighth month they halted in the suburbs, waited for more troops, then advanced to the old walls of Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 凡三日，聞思烈軍潰，即夜棄輜重馳還。

translations.literal: In all three days they heard Si Lie's army had collapsed; that night they abandoned baggage and raced back.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later word came that Si Lie's force had routed; that night they abandoned their supplies and fled.

sentences.zh: 黎明至鄭門，聚軍乃入。

translations.literal: At dawn they reached the Zheng Gate, gathered the army, and then entered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they reached the Zheng Gate, rallied the troops, and entered the city.

sentences.zh: 言者謂：「合喜始則抗命不出，中則逗遛不進，終則棄軍先遁，委棄軍資不可勝計，不斬之無以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Speakers said, "Hexi at first resisted orders and would not set out; in the middle he lingered and would not advance; in the end he abandoned the army and fled first. The military supplies he abandoned were beyond calculation. If he is not beheaded, there is no way to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Speakers said, "Hexi at first resisted orders and would not set out; in the middle he lingered and would not advance; in the end he abandoned the army and fled first. The military supplies he abandoned were beyond calculation. If he is not beheaded, there is no way to answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 上貸其死，免爲庶人，既而籍其家以賜軍士。

translations.literal: The emperor spared his life, reduced him to commoner status, and soon registered his household property to bestow on the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared his life but reduced him to commoner rank, then confiscated his estate for the troops.

sentences.zh: 既廢，居汴中，常鞅鞅不樂。

translations.literal: Having been removed from office, he dwelt in Bian and was often discontent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed, he remained in Bian, sour and restless.

sentences.zh: 會大將速不泬遣人招之，合喜即治裝欲行，崔立邀至省酌酒餞送，且以白金二百兩爲贐。

translations.literal: It happened that the great general Subutai sent men to summon him; Hexi at once prepared his baggage intending to go; Cui Li invited him to the Department to pour wine and send him off, and moreover gave two hundred taels of white silver as parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: Subutai sent envoys to summon him; Hexi packed to go. Cui Li invited him to the Department for a farewell feast and gave him two hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 明日，復詣省別立，方對語，適一人自歸德持文書至，發視之，乃行省傳哀宗語以諭合喜者，其言曰：「卿朕老臣，中間雖廢出，未嘗忘卿。

translations.literal: Next day he again went to the Department to take leave of Li; as they were conversing, a man happened to arrive from Guide with documents; opening and viewing them, it was the Branch Secretariat transmitting Emperor Aizong's words to instruct Hexi; the words said: "You are my old minister; though removed in between, I have never forgotten you.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he went again to bid Cui Li farewell. As they spoke, a courier arrived from Guide with a dispatch from the Branch Secretariat bearing Emperor Aizong's message: "You are an old servant of mine; though you were dismissed, I have not forgotten you.

sentences.zh: 今崔立已變，卿處舊人尚多，若能反正，與卿世襲公相。」

translations.literal: Now Cui Li has already rebelled. There are still many old loyalists where you are. If you can return to correctness, hereditary offices of duke and minister will be yours."
translations.idiomatic: Now Cui Li has already rebelled. There are still many old loyalists where you are. If you can return to correctness, hereditary offices of duke and minister will be yours."

sentences.zh: 立怒，叱左右系之獄，是日斬之。

translations.literal: Li grew angry, shouted to attendants to bind him into prison, and that day beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li's face darkened. He had Hexi seized and beheaded that same day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：合喜初年用兵西夏，屢著勞效，要亦諸將顏盞蝦蟆等功也。

translations.literal: Commentary: In Hexi's early years campaigning against Western Xia he repeatedly showed merit in labor and effect—yet in the main this too was the merit of generals such as Yanzhan Xiami.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In his youth Hexi campaigned fruitfully against Western Xia—though the credit owed more to generals like Yanzhan Xiami.

sentences.zh: 既當大任，遂自矜伐，汴城之役，舉措煩擾，質出兵退，即圖稱賀，此豈有體國之誠心者乎。

translations.literal: Once he bore great responsibility he became self-congratulatory and boastful; in the Bian city campaign his measures were vexing and troublesome; when the enemy army truly withdrew he at once plotted congratulations—was this a man with sincere mind to cherish the state?
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated he grew vain; at Bian his counsels were a nuisance, and when the enemy withdrew he sought triumphal honors—was that loyalty to the realm?

sentences.zh: 中牟之潰，衆怒所歸，幸逭一死，猶懷異圖，卒殞猜疑，天蓋假手于崔立也。

translations.literal: When Zhongmou collapsed he became the object of the masses' wrath; fortunate to escape death, he yet harbored contrary designs; in the end he perished in suspicion—and Heaven surely used Cui Li's hand.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongmou he bore the army's hatred, survived by grace, yet plotted anew—and Heaven, it seems, killed him through Cui Li's hand.
